newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on technical slip, spreading.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on technical slip, spreading.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on a technical setback plus corn/wheat spreading, traders said.
"We have had a nice rally and it's correcting," said Dave Armstrong, analyst for ABN Amro, The Chicago Corp.

The contract low in September of $3.21 per bushel was set on July 8 in a seasonal harvest slide amid reports of excellent winter wheat yields this year in the U.S. and virtually disease-free new crop wheat. Since then, September rallied roughly 40 cents per bushel in a race back to six-week highs, partially pulled up by occasional strength in corn and soy complex futures, and was showing overbought signals on charts.
The nine-day relative strength index for the September had been flirting with the 70 percent level, an area considered overbought by short-term traders.
Corn/wheat spreading and some unwinding of wheat/corn spreads set during the bulk of wheat harvesting were noted.
The recent rally in prices also brought in increased hedge selling pressure, traders said.
Wheat closed 1/4 to 2-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with September down 1-3/4 at $3.56-1/4.

Refco Inc sold four million bushels of December, and LIT America sold one million December as did Merrill Lynch Futures, traders said. Rand Financial bought two million December and Prudential Securities bought one million bushels of December, traders said.
In spread trading, FIMAT Futures did one million bushels of December/September at 14 cents, premium December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 18,000 contracts, about the same as the 18,023 traded Tuesday.
In wheat options, Cargill Investor Services bought 200 Dectember $3.50 calls at 14 cents and sold 200 September $3.50 puts at six cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000 contracts, below the 8,578 traded Tuesday.
